& \sqrt N E^{\Pi}[\|\theta- \theta_{0}\|_{H^{-k-2}} 1_{\{\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-k-2}} > 1\}}|Z^{(N)}] \\
&\le \sqrt N \big(E^{\Pi}[\|\theta- \theta_{0}\|_{L^2}^2|Z^{(N)}])^{1/2} \Pi(\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{L^2}> 1 |Z^{(N)})\big)^{1/2} =O_{P_{\theta_0}^\mathbb N}\big( e^{-bN \delta_N^2/2}\tilde \delta_N N^{1/2} \big).

issues.failure_explanation: The split at radius 1 around vartheta_0 = sqrt(N)(theta_0 - T) places the bulk of both laws tau_N and bar tau_N (which concentrate at scale O_P(1) around vartheta_0, as the Bernstein-von Mises limit shows) into the two tail integrals, so those integrals are not small. In the second term the event {sqrt(N)||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} > 1} is replaced by the strictly smaller event {||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} > 1} (dropping the factor sqrt(N)), and the probability is then bounded by Pi(||theta-theta_0||_{L^2} > 1 | Z); but the true event {||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} > N^{-1/2}} has posterior probability tending to one (the contraction rate delta_tilde_N(0) is much larger than N^{-1/2}), and the true second term tends to the positive constant E[||Z|| 1_{||Z||>1}] for Z ~ N_{theta_0}, not o_P(1). Likewise the third term is not eventually zero: on bar Theta_N only the unscaled error ||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} < 1 is known, while the scaled error sqrt(N)||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} is O_P(1) and not < 1. As written, the displayed estimates do not establish the claimed O_P(e^{-c N delta_N^2}) bound.

failure_location.quote: Finally, by definition of $\bar \Theta_N$ and since $\tilde \delta_N=o(1)$, we have $\Pi^{\bar \Theta_N}(\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-k-2}}> 1 |Z^{(N)})=0$ from some $N$ onwards so the third term equals zero eventually, and the result is proved.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the radius-1 splitting by the standard coupling that pairs the common part bar Theta_N exactly and pays only for the exceptional set: W_1(tau_N, bar tau_N) <= sqrt(N) E^Pi[||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}} 1_{bar Theta_N^c} | Z] + 2 Pi(bar Theta_N^c|Z) * sqrt(N) E^{Pi^{bar Theta_N}}||theta-theta_0||_{H^{-k-2}}, which is O_P(e^{-cN delta_N^2}) by Theorem postcont. This is a short, local repair preserving the statement, the rate, and all downstream results.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition wassconv does not establish its stated bound, so the transfer from the localised and recentred posterior to the full posterior used in the proof of Theorem mainbvm (and transitively bvminv and ganzwien) is unsupported as written. The proposition's statement itself is true, so no final theorem is lost once the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Proposition wassconv: the radius-1 tail splitting does not bound W_1(tau_N, bar tau_N); both tail terms are mis-estimated
issues.why_classification: The proposition's statement and exponential rate are correct and are all that downstream results use; the repair is a short, standard coupling argument replacing the failed tail split, with no loss of any claim, rate, or regime.

issues.failure_explanation: With J_N ≃ N delta_N^2 = N^{d/(2 gamma+d)}, the quantity sqrt(N) delta_N^2 J_N^{gamma - kappa_bar} equals N^{[gamma(d-1) + d/2 - d kappa_bar]/(2 gamma+d)}, not N^{-(kappa_bar - d/2)/(2 gamma+d)} as displayed (the two agree only for d=1). Convergence to zero therefore requires kappa_bar in (gamma(d-1)/d + 1/2, gamma); combined with (ks) (kappa_bar < kappa - d/2, kappa < k - d/2) this forces k > gamma(d-1)/d + d + 1/2. This is not implied by the hypothesis k > max(zeta + 5d/2, eta_0) of Theorem mainbvm nor by the 'any k > 3d' of Theorem bvminv: e.g. d=2, gamma=9, k=7 satisfies both but admits no admissible (kappa, kappa_bar), and then the displayed Cameron-Martin bound diverges like N^{(gamma(d-1)+d/2-d kappa_bar)/(2 gamma+d)} > 0. Hence the density ratio in (postbus0)-(postbus000) is not shown to tend to one for such k, and the Laplace approximation in Theorem laplaceapp, and consequently Theorems mainbvm and bvminv in H^{-k-2}, are unproved for k <= gamma(d-1)/d + d + 1/2.

failure_location.quote: $$\frac{|t|}{\sqrt N} |\langle \theta, p_N (\bar \psi_{\theta_0})\rangle_{\mathcal H_N}| \lesssim |t| \delta_N K_{N, \bar \kappa} \lesssim |t| \delta_N^2 \sqrt N J_N^{\gamma-\bar \kappa} = N^{-(\bar \kappa -d/2)/(2\gamma+d)} \to 0$$ as $N \to \infty$, in view of (\ref{approxrkhs}) and the choice of $\bar \kappa$ in (\ref{ks}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis on k to k > max(zeta + 5d/2, eta_0, gamma(d-1)/d + d + 1/2) and choose kappa, kappa_bar with kappa_bar in (gamma(d-1)/d + 1/2, gamma); then the Cameron-Martin exponent is negative and the ratio in (postbus0) tends to one. This is a limited weakening of the k-range of Theorems mainbvm and bvminv that leaves recognisably comparable results and keeps all applications, including Theorem ganzwien, intact.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems mainbvm and bvminv overclaim the range of the Sobolev index k: the BvM in H^{-k-2} is not established for small k (for d >= 2, bvminv's 'any k > 3d' includes values, e.g. k=7 when d=2 and gamma=9, for which the proof fails). The paper's main result Theorem ganzwien is unaffected because it may use any sufficiently large k via Theorem bvminv.
issues.title: Theorem laplaceapp: the Cameron-Martin density bound has the wrong exponent and silently requires k larger than assumed in Theorems mainbvm and bvminv
issues.why_classification: The repair necessarily restricts the range of the central quantifier k in Theorems mainbvm and bvminv (the topology of the BvM), so it is more than a local fix and loses a (small) advertised regime; however a limited weakening suffices, no new proof architecture is needed, and the main result ganzwien survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated sigma_N^2 ≡ delta_tilde_N(zeta)^2 + 1/N (so sigma_N ≈ delta_tilde_N(zeta), since delta_tilde_N(zeta)^2 >> 1/N), the first chaining term equals sqrt(N) ∫_0^{sigma_N} u^{-d/2 beta} du = sqrt(N) sigma_N^{1-d/2 beta}/(1-d/2 beta) ≈ sqrt(N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{1-d/2 beta}, which diverges because (1-d/2 beta) * gamma(gamma_bar - zeta)/((gamma_bar+1)(2 gamma+d)) < 1/2 always; it is not ≲ sqrt(N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{2-d/beta} as claimed. Similarly the second term is of order sqrt(log N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{1-d/beta}/sqrt(N) (the displayed order also drops the factor 1/sqrt(N)), not sqrt(log N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{1-2d/beta}. The displayed orders are exactly what follows from the sharp quadratic variance of Condition gemol C), ||g_{theta,psi}||_{L^2(X)} ≤ c||theta_{(t,psi)} - theta_0||^4_{L^2}, i.e. sigma_N ≈ delta_tilde_N(zeta)^2, which makes sigma_N/delta_tilde_N(zeta) ≈ delta_tilde_N(zeta) and yields precisely sqrt(N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{2-d/beta} and sqrt(log N) delta_tilde_N(zeta)^{1-2d/beta}/sqrt(N), both o(1) under the hypotheses (beta > 2d).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the variance estimate by the Condition C bound E f_{theta,psi}^2(Z) = ||g_{theta,psi}||^2_{L^2(X)} ≤ c ||theta_{(t,psi)} - theta_0||^4_{L^2} ≲ delta_tilde_N(zeta)^4 + 1/N ≡ sigma_N^2; then sigma_N/delta_tilde_N(zeta) ≈ delta_tilde_N(zeta) and the displayed orders follow and are o(1) under the stated hypotheses. No other part of the argument needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of Lemma oldtimer does not establish the o(1) bounds for the stochastic remainders R_{t,N} and W_{t,N}, which are the key inputs to Theorem laplaceapp and hence, transitively, to Theorems mainbvm, bvminv and ganzwien. The lemma's statement is true, and a one-line replacement of the variance bound repairs the proof without changing any conclusion or rate.
issues.title: Lemma oldtimer: the variance bound via Condition B is inconsistent with the chaining orders used to conclude o(1)
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement and every downstream result survive a one-line local repair (sharpening the variance via Condition C); no claim, rate, or regime is lost, and no new lemma or reoptimization is needed.
